answer: Each identity posts one quote on the harbor book, locking an 80-credit bond and 100 credits inventory key-bound for one horizon. The harbor publishes a pulse, and an auditor recomputes the book; a quote whose spread, inventory, or horizon mismatches its key loses its bond. Fees rise with order: the kth quote pays 15+2(k-1); the 1000th pays 2013; 1000 fakes pay 1,014,000 plus 180,000 locked. A quote-copying ring fails because copying one honest quote repeats its hash and horizon, which the auditor catches. An honest agent locks 80 once, pays 15 once, and recovers both after a clean horizon.
